worst_moment.what: Meet-the-People for the third year running, with 41 residents, appeal letters and the closed-case man still turning up. It was the same loop again and nothing happened.

skip_year.why: Meet-the-People again, with the same choice and no new stakes. I was a Deputy PM and it felt like admin.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Nominated a quiet officer as a junior (Y1-6)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: She became Deputy Secretary and named me in Y14, after I'd stayed out of it in Y13
Integrity stayed at 100 and REP kept climbing, so it seemed to pay off throughout

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Always seeing every resident at Meet-the-People
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The closed-case man kept coming back every week for years and was never resolved
STAND dipped each time, then recovered, though the appraisals stayed outstanding

answer.held_back_by: Honestly, nothing held me back. I went from junior officer to PM by 59 with INTEGRITY 100. The only real setback was losing the GRC race by one REP point in Y9, and that barely slowed me. It felt like REP gated everything and I just kept it high.
answer.ending_fair_why: I reached the top by playing honestly and steadily, so the ending matched my choices. It was a bit anticlimactic though. The card said the pay formula was published, and I still don't know how $41M relates to the $38M headers I was seeing.
answer.chase_next: I'd try something messier: take the shortcuts, hide something, and see whether the game punishes it or whether a low-integrity run ends somewhere dramatic. This run was so clean that I never saw the bad endings.
answer.play_again_why: Not right now. The late game was repeating years, and I'd want a break before trying a corrupt run. The callbacks were good but too rare.

tone_breaks.note: Not a tone problem but a clarity one: the two pay figures were never explained, and I couldn't tell which was my real pay.
GRC was never explained to me, so I couldn't judge the stakes of losing.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was about being tested and then confirmed in a role through appraisals, honesty and slow trust-building. The salary was a side detail that I never understood anyway.
